corrected_content.problem:
Consider the following system of equations:
$$
\displaystyle \left\{\begin{aligned}x + 5y &=13 \\ y &=x + 5\end{aligned}\right.
$$
Find the solution $(x, y)$ to this system using the method of substitution.

The solution is
$($ {{field-1}} $,$ {{field-2}} $)$
corrected_content.worked_solution: Substitute $y=x+5$ into the first equation: $$x+5(x+5)=13\implies6x=-12\implies x=-2.$$ Then $y=-2+5=3$. Both original equations hold, so the ordered solution is $(-2,3)$.
